citation.title: Achievements and lessons learned from the operation of KSTAR plasma control system upgrade
citation.authors: S.-h. Hahn, B.G. Penaflor, P.G. Milne, et al.

topic: Hardware, operating-system and data-acquisition upgrade of the KSTAR plasma control system in 2016. The paper reports latency tests and operational use.
own_question: Whether the upgraded PCS can acquire and control reliably for long pulses, and what latency it adds.
actual_method_and_evidence: Loopback and full-path echo tests report about 300 μs round-trip latency and about 200±50 μs one-way processing. A longer real-time EFIT iteration count is compared with CCD boundary estimates in 2016 operation. The paper contains no CES, BES, ECEI or temperature nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The KSTAR PCS runs real-time magnetics-based control, including rtEFIT, with sub-millisecond I/O latency in its 2016 configuration.
claim_checks.qualification: Describes the 2016 PCS configuration only. It does not report the 2022 configuration or the CES/BES/ECEI pathway. No 10 ms nowcast deployment is shown.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Reported latencies are for magnetics and coil I/O. Report arrival times for profile diagnostics are not given.
validation_if_relevant: Hardware-in-the-loop tests and the 2016 campaign. There is no ML validation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not use this source to claim that our estimator is deployable in real time.
Do not use it to claim that CES reports are available within PCS latency.
Do not use it to claim that it covers the KSTAR2022 hardware.
Do not use it to claim that it demonstrates any temperature estimation.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most, cite this source briefly as context on the KSTAR real-time control infrastructure. It is not evidence for our problem or targets.
